Hey all,
Bit of a noob here with nvim setup. I'm using mini.statusline but whenever a file is nested a few levels, the displayed path is too long to be of any use to me. I've used what very little knowledge I have to try to truncate it, but I ended up accidentally messing up completely, so here I am:
how can I configure it to truncate the path 🙏

comment_data.body:
Would you mind elaborating on what you mean by "truncate the path"?

Currently 'mini.statusline' does the following to make working with long paths better:
- It focuses on the later part of the path, so file's basename has more priority.
- It switches from full to relative path if window is [140 columns wide or less](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/b1af49d98233180c6045e81f4aef5b663d032b62/doc/mini-statusline.txt#L92). This usually results in shorter path shown as it drops the "current working directory prefix". You can usually see the effect by creating one or several vertical splits (`<C-w><C-v>`).

reply_data.body:
> Typically I already know most of the path since I told nvim to open there, and I only need to know the path relative to the project root (or the option to, only so a blind man like myself can quickly see the important part of the path).

If always showing path relative to *current working directory* (i.e. the directory you opened Neovim in or after doing `:cd`) is enough for you, then you can override active 'mini.statusline' content like so:

```lua
local content_active = function()
  local mode, mode_hl = MiniStatusline.section_mode({ trunc_width = 120 })
  local git = MiniStatusline.section_git({ trunc_width = 40 })
  local diff = MiniStatusline.section_diff({ trunc_width = 75 })
  local diagnostics = MiniStatusline.section_diagnostics({ trunc_width = 75 })
  local lsp = MiniStatusline.section_lsp({ trunc_width = 75 })
  -- Always show truncated file name (i.e. relative to current working directory)
  local filename = MiniStatusline.section_filename({ trunc_width = 9999 })
  local fileinfo = MiniStatusline.section_fileinfo({ trunc_width = 120 })
  local location = MiniStatusline.section_location({ trunc_width = 75 })
  local search = MiniStatusline.section_searchcount({ trunc_width = 75 })

  return MiniStatusline.combine_groups({
    { hl = mode_hl, strings = { mode } },
    { hl = 'MiniStatuslineDevinfo', strings = { git, diff, diagnostics, lsp } },
    '%<', -- Mark general truncate point
    { hl = 'MiniStatuslineFilename', strings = { filename } },
    '%=', -- End left alignment
    { hl = 'MiniStatuslineFileinfo', strings = { fileinfo } },
    { hl = mode_hl, strings = { search, location } },
  })
end
require('mini.statusline').setup({ content = { active = content_active } })
```

Dynamically truncating file path to be like "L../M../c../P../s../b../functional/currying/notes-and-reviews.md"  is possible, but it will be slow or requires a cache. Statusline updates *very* frequently so speed is very important here.

Does this help?
